doe_award.program: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law grant (first set of BIL-funded projects)

rows.reason: Page states 'nearly $150 million grant' from DOE, first set of projects under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Albemarle's Kings Mountain, North Carolina, location. The exact $149.7M is not on the page, and the page does not name the Battery Materials Processing program, so the program text is corrected to what the page says. Status check: DOE's March 2026 Final EA/FONSI (DOE/EA-2265, https://www.energy.gov/node/4857066) treats the grant as continuing at about $149M federal share; no termination found in one search of the Oct 2025 cancellations.

Page states grant of up to $220m from DOE under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Battery Materials Processing and Battery Manufacturing grant, for 'its Vidalia active anode material (AAM) facility in Louisiana'. State and facility name on page; city comes from the facility name. Status check: no termination found in one search; Syrah's Sept 2026 quarterly materials mention restricted Vidalia cash subject to DOE approval and slower-than-expected binding funding documents, but nothing shows the grant cancelled.

doe_award.program: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law grant (specific DOE program not named on the page)

rows.reason: Page states NOVONIX finalized its US$100 million DOE grant, funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, for its Riverside facility in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The page does not name a specific DOE program, so the row's 'Battery Materials Processing' label is softened. Status check: no termination found in one search; a later report says about $51.3M of the grant remained to claim.

Cited page (Feb 2023) supports a $2B ATVM conditional commitment for a $3.5B 'McCarren, Nevada' factory (page spells McCarren). But the commitment never closed: Waste Dive (Apr 2025) reports Redwood 'decided to discontinue its agreement with the federal government last year without drawing any funds' (https://www.wastedive.com/news/international-recycling-group-erie-project-cancel-licycle-doe-loans/744450/), and Yahoo/Reuters (May 19, 2025) lists Redwood's battery factory among seven conditional commitments DOE planned to cancel, noting it was 'previously cancelled by the company' (https://www.yahoo.com/news/us-plans-cancel-7-conditional-152451125.html). So 'announced' with an LPO award is wrong: the conditional commitment was withdrawn before any draw.

Page states a contracted DOE grant of over $55 million under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Battery Materials Processing and Battery Manufacturing Program (Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains) for BWM's Bartlesville, Oklahoma facility. Status check: HigherGov lists the $55.19M award as ongoing (modified Feb 2026) and a Nov 2025 Business Wire release marks the expansion start; no termination found.
